overview: This bill creates the Fort Ontario Holocaust Refugee Shelter National Historical Park in New York as part of the National Park System. The park would preserve and tell the story of the 982 refugees from World War II who were housed at Fort Ontario from August 1944 to February 1946, people who had fled the Holocaust in Europe. The park would be formally established only once the Interior Department has acquired enough land within the proposed boundary to manage it, and land owned by the state or local governments could be added only by donation. The bill also designates America's National Churchill Museum at Westminster College in Fulton, Missouri, as a National Historic Landmark, allows the Interior Department to partner with and assist groups there without limiting what the property owners can do, and orders a study of whether the site should become a national park unit. The Senate passed it on December 16, 2025, and as of December 17, 2025, it was awaiting action in the House.
for: Supporters say the bill preserves an important and little-known chapter of World War II history and recognizes a museum devoted to Winston Churchill, while protecting local landowners' control.
against: Critics say adding new park units and landmarks increases long-term costs for a National Park Service that already has a large backlog of maintenance needs.
